newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nippon Oil to boost Australia coal sales.
newsitem.headline: Nippon Oil to boost Australia coal sales.

text.p: Nippon Oil Co Ltd said on Monday it planned to boost sales of Australian coal to Japan's electric power utilities.

The oil refiner, which has equity stakes in two Australian coal firms, plans to sell a total of four million tonnes of Australian coal this fiscal year, which began on April 1, up about 29 percent from the previous year, a Nippon Oil spokesman said.
By fiscal 2000/01, Nippon Oil plans to sell about five million tonnes of Australian coal per year, he said.
Nippon Oil has roughly a 10 percent interest in Bayswater Colliery Co Pty Ltd and a 20 percent interest in Oakbridge Pty Ltd, the spokesman said.
Nippon Oil's coal sales are divided equally between the steel industry, electric utilities and other industries.
In recent years, Nippon Oil's coal sales have suffered from a downturn in demand from Japanese steel makers, which have been reducing steel production.
Coal demand from electric utilities, however, is forecast to rise due to an increase in coal-fuelled power plants, the Nippon Oil spokesman said.

Japan's electric utilities plan to expand the capacity of their coal-fired power plants to around 43.5 million kilowatts by 2006/07, accounting for about 15.7 percent of utilities' total power generating capacity, up from current levels of 20.3 million kw or 9.8 percent.
Japan relies on Australia for more than half of its coal imports.
